best_for: Streamers, teachers and anyone recording a screen or camera on Windows, Mac or Linux who wants a free tool with scenes and live switching, and will spend an evening learning it.
description:
OBS Studio is free, open source software for video recording and live streaming. Lain created it and maintains it, with help from a wide group of contributors, and it works with all the common streaming platforms.

You can set hotkeys for nearly anything: switching scenes, starting or stopping a stream or recording, muting a source, or push to talk. Between scenes you can pick a transition or play your own stinger video. The window is built from docks you can move around, or pop out into their own windows. Adding a source is quick, and you can duplicate one you already set up. When something goes wrong, there is a knowledge base, forums and a Discord server.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: OBS Studio costs nothing and is released under the GPL. The project is paid for by sponsors and backers through Open Collective, Patreon and GitHub.

points.title: Scenes you switch live
points.text: You build any number of scenes from window captures, images, text, browser windows, webcams and capture cards, then switch with custom transitions. Studio Mode lets you check a scene before it goes live, and Multiview shows up to 8 scenes at once.

points.title: Audio cleanup built in
points.text: The mixer has per-source filters such as noise gate, noise suppression and gain, and it loads VST plugins. Good enough to tame a cheap microphone without extra software.

points.title: Plugins moved in 33.0
points.text: OBS takes native plugins plus Lua and Python scripts. Version 33.0 moved third-party plugins to a new folder layout; the old locations keep working until 34.0, so check your plugins before that update.

points.title: Operating system floors
points.text: Windows 10 and 11 are supported, and macOS 13 or later, with separate Intel and Apple silicon builds. On Linux the official route is the Flathub Flatpak, verified as published by the OBS Project (x64 here), or a PPA for Ubuntu 26.04 and newer; 33.0 dropped Ubuntu 24.04.

points.title: Arm64 Windows means the zip
points.text: The Windows installer is x64 and installs for all users. Windows on Arm users get a zip package instead, also listed here.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 48 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
